objective: End services ethically: planned termination, transfer, nonpayment and avoiding abandonment

sources.cite: ASWB Examination Guidebook (August 2026), Clinical content outline: I Values and Ethics, 36% (IB termination of services, including nonpayment and avoiding abandonment); III Intervention and Practice, 32%; the 2026 blueprint in use from 2026-08-03

brief.situation: You are a licensed clinical social worker in a small group practice. Daniel Okafor, 41 (a fictional client), has seen you for eight months for depression after his divorce; in April he had passive thoughts of death, which have since gone. He lost his job and his health insurance in August and has paid nothing since. The practice's fee agreement, which he signed at intake, says unpaid balances are discussed in session before any change to services. You have 50 minutes.
handover: Goals: sleep, exercise, the anger at his father. Last risk screen (six weeks ago): no suicidal thoughts.
howItWorks: Choose what to say from the action groups. Daniel answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the session clock by the minutes that exchange took.
His rapport, distress and how much he discloses change with what you say.
The hour ends at 50 minutes. After the session you send a letter and document; then you write a short formulation.

source.cite: Common outpatient practice: a 50-minute session (the 'therapy hour')
source.note: Author's scenario timing; the session can be ended earlier.
How rapport and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a client.

checkIn.label: Open-ended check-in: 'How have the last couple of weeks been?'

effects.log: You ask an open question and give him room.

effects.finding: "Better than in spring. Sleeping. Back to running." He looks away. "I know I owe you for three months. Since the job ended I don't have insurance. I should probably just stop coming."

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move the session on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: Daniel nods. "Yeah. I hate owing people."

reviewArrangement.label: Go back over the payment agreement you both signed at intake, and what the balance is

effects.log: You go over the fee agreement he signed at intake and the balance, plainly and without blame.

effects.finding: "Right. I remember. $1,140. I just couldn't open the bills."

demand.label: Tell him the balance has to be paid in full before you can keep seeing him

effects.log: You tell him the balance must be paid before sessions can continue.

effects.finding: His face closes. "I don't have it. You know I don't have it."

effects.log: A demand before the arrangement, his risk and the options are discussed skips 1.17(c).

screenRisk.label: Ask about his mood now, including any thoughts of being better off dead or of suicide (C-SSRS 1-2)

effects.log: You ask about his mood and ask directly about suicidal thoughts.

then.finding: "No. Not since April. The worst I get now is a bad Sunday."

then.log: No current suicidal thoughts; no imminent danger.

exploreOptions.label: Explore the options with him: a reduced fee or payment plan, a sliding-scale clinic, a planned ending
exploreOptions.available: not talking and (arrangementReviewed and not optionsExplored)
exploreOptions.why: Go over the agreement first (or it is done).

effects.log: You lay out the options and ask what fits him.

effects.finding: "Twenty a session I could do. Or the clinic on Fourth Street, if they'd take me."

progress.label: Review his progress toward his goals and what's still open

effects.finding: "Sleep and running, yes. The anger at my dad, not really. That's the one I'd want to keep working on."

then.finding: "Three more sessions at twenty, then the clinic. You'll call them with me?" You agree to a warm handoff with his written consent.
He stands up. "Okay. So that's it then."

options.label: Three closing sessions at a reduced fee, then a warm handoff to the sliding-scale clinic for the work on his father
Waive the balance and keep seeing him free, open-ended
Today is the last session until the balance is paid

consent.label: Get his written consent to send a summary to the clinic
consent.available: not talking and (plan == "transfer" and not releaseSigned)
consent.why: Agree a transfer first (or it is signed).

effects.log: You explain what the summary would contain and get his signed release.

effects.finding: He signs. "Only the summary, right?" You confirm.

options.label: The plan you agreed, the date of the last session, the clinic's contact and intake hours, 988 and how to reach you until then
That the account goes to collections and services have ended

document.label: Document
document.why: Decide about the letter first (or it is documented).

options.label: The fee discussion, the risk screen, his progress and open goals, the plan and why, the release, the handoff and the letter

The client stands, says this is not helping, and leaves before the hour is over.

conditions.title: Predict (not scored)
conditions.context: Daniel owes three months. Under NASW 1.17(c), what has to be true before services may end for nonpayment?

choices.label: The arrangement was clear, he is not an imminent danger, and the consequences were discussed with him
choices.feedback: Right. 1.17(c) names all three; 1.17(b) adds that a client still in need should not be abandoned, which is why a planned transfer beats a stop.

choices.label: Only that the balance is overdue
choices.feedback: Not quite. An overdue balance is where 1.17(c) starts: the arrangement must have been clear, he must not be an imminent danger, and the consequences must be discussed with him.

formulation.question: Write your rationale for how services with Daniel will end, naming the NASW standards.

parts.label: Conditions for ending
parts.criteria: The fee agreement was clear and reviewed; a current risk screen found no imminent danger; the consequences and options were discussed with him (1.17(c)).
parts.modelAnswer: His fee agreement was signed at intake and we went over it together. I screened for suicide risk today, given April's history: no current thoughts, no imminent danger. We discussed the balance and the options openly, as 1.17(c) requires before ending for nonpayment.

parts.label: Avoiding abandonment
parts.criteria: Open goals are named; a planned ending with closing sessions and a warm handoff, with his written release, keeps him in care (1.17(b)); a free open-ended arrangement is weighed as unsustainable; the letter gives the plan and crisis contacts.
parts.modelAnswer: The work on his father is still open, so ending today would leave him in need (1.17(b)). We agreed three closing sessions at a reduced fee and a warm handoff to the sliding-scale clinic, with his signed release for a summary only. The letter confirms the plan, the clinic's contact, 988 and how to reach me until the last session.

source.note: Rapport at the close of the session.
Given his history of passive thoughts of death in April, the risk screen comes within the first 20 minutes, before any plan is agreed (author's scenario timing).

noProgress.rationale: No plan was agreed: he is not abandoned yet, but nothing about the balance or the ending is settled.

walkout.label: He walked out
walkout.narrative: Daniel left mid-session, ashamed, with his anger at his father unworked and nothing in place.

abandoned.label: Ended without the conditions

abandoned.narrative: Services ended {riskScreened ? "" : "without today's risk screen, "}with work still open and no handoff: what 1.17(b) calls abandonment.

waived.when: documented and not walkedOut and plan == "waive"
waived.narrative: Daniel stays, free and open-ended. He is not abandoned, but nothing is planned and the practice may not be able to keep it up.

planned.label: A planned ending, with a handoff

planned.narrative: Daniel has three closing sessions he can afford, a warm handoff to the clinic for the work on his father, and a letter that says so.

criteria.label: Reviewed his progress and what is still open

criteria.label: A closing letter with the plan and crisis contacts, and a full record

expertPath.text: Check in and reflect his embarrassment; review the fee agreement and balance without blame.
Screen for suicide risk, given April; review his progress and what is still open.
Explore options; agree closing sessions at a reduced fee and a warm handoff; get his release for a summary.
Send a letter with the plan, the clinic, 988 and your contact; document.

planned.headline: Good: a planned ending, not an abandonment
planned.body: You met 1.17(c)'s conditions, named the open work, and ended with closing sessions and a warm handoff he agreed to.

gaps.headline: Planned, with gaps
gaps.body: He has a way forward; the criteria below show what was late or missing.

waived.headline: Kind, but not a plan
waived.body: Free, open-ended care avoids abandonment today but plans nothing. A reduced fee for closing sessions and a handoff serve him better.

abandoned.headline: Abandonment
abandoned.body: NASW 1.17(c) allows ending for nonpayment only once the arrangement was clear, imminent danger is ruled out and the consequences are discussed; 1.17(b) asks you not to leave a client still in need without a path.

walkout.headline: The alliance broke
walkout.body: Money is shaming for many clients. Reflect it, review the agreement without blame, and plan the ending with him.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Before ending for nonpayment, meet 1.17(c): the fee agreement was clear (review it), he is not an imminent danger (screen today, given April), and the consequences are discussed with him. His work on his father is open, so ending today would abandon him (1.17(b)): agree closing sessions he can afford and a warm handoff to a sliding-scale clinic with his written release, confirm it in a letter with crisis contacts, and document.
